stem: A Massachusetts pharmacy has prescription pads printed with its own name and address and supplies them free of charge to a nearby prescriber. There is no agreement of any kind between them, nothing of value passes, and no patient is ever sent to the pharmacy as a result. What is the pharmacy's position?

choices.text: Compliant, because nothing of value passed to the prescriber.
Compliant, because no patient was in fact steered to the pharmacy.
Compliant, provided the prescriber stays free to send prescriptions elsewhere.
In violation, because supplying forms that refer to a pharmacy is prohibited.
In violation, but only where the forms are used for controlled substances.

explanation.core_reasoning: 247 CMR 9.01(14) states that a licensee may not provide any practitioner with blank prescription forms which refer to any pharmacist or pharmacy. The violation is complete on providing the forms. Nothing turns on payment, on an agreement, or on whether any patient was actually steered.

choice_analysis.A: The prohibition has no remuneration element, unlike 247 CMR 9.01(11).
choice_analysis.C: The prescriber's freedom of choice is irrelevant to the prohibition.
choice_analysis.D: Correct: the pre-printed reference to the pharmacy is the violation.
choice_analysis.E: The prohibition is not limited by schedule.

related_facts: 247 CMR 9.01(11) separately prohibits remuneration for referrals
explanation.mpje_trap: Candidates import the remuneration element of the neighbouring anti-kickback provision into a prohibition that has none.

reasoning_steps: Identify that the forms carry a reference to a pharmacy
Note that the pharmacy provided them to a practitioner
Apply 247 CMR 9.01(14) without looking for value or for steering
